summary.title: Fail-safe edge-AI vision dishwasher-picker robot
summary.description: Fail-safe dish-picking system: an ABB YuMi unloads cups using YOLO11n-seg vision. Inference runs on a cloud model (primary), a Raspberry Pi 5 (secondary) and a Westermo Lynx switch (tertiary), degrading to a safe stop. All camera access and robot jobs pass through one Robot Gateway. The model describes the laboratory deployment as implemented in the repository; threat status Mitigated is used only where the code implements, and the tests check, the mitigation.

diagrams.title: Gatewayed STRIDE

data.name: Internet trust boundary
data.description: Separates the cloud inference service from the laboratory. In the intended design the primary model runs as a cloud service reached over the internet. In the current laboratory set-up a MacBook Pro on the lab network stands in for the cloud, and the lab network has no internet connection, so the threats on flows crossing this boundary describe the intended deployment.

data.name:
Westermo Lynx switch
(WeOS Application Hosting)
data.description: Container on the Westermo Lynx-3510 switch. The Lynx also switches all lab traffic and powers the camera over PoE. Hosted applications share a capped part of the switch's CPU and memory.

data.name: Raspberry Pi 5 host (Docker, host network)
data.description: The Raspberry Pi 5 runs the gateway container and, in the current set-up, the secondary inference client. Anything that compromises the Pi host affects both. Gateway configuration, the token registry and the calibration file live in the container.

data.name:
Robot cell devices
(lab OT network)
data.description: Devices that act on or observe the physical cell. Both are reachable by any device connected to the lab network; neither authenticates its clients beyond the controller's default RWS account.

data.name:
Robot Gateway
(FastAPI)
data.description: Single entry point to the robot and the camera (repo gateway/). REST API under /api/v1 over plain HTTP on port 8000. Strict mode: bearer token, SHA-256 hash looked up in the client registry; permissions robot.read, robot.control, camera.read, camera.control. One control lease (5 s, higher priority pre-empts). Validates RWS move targets against a safe zone (flange, x 180..800, y -400..500, z 50..600 mm) and speed 1..1500 mm/s. Refuses camera frames older than 5 s. Runs in Docker with --restart unless-stopped.

threats.title: Compromise of the gateway host or process
threats.description: An attacker gains code execution in the gateway container or on the Raspberry Pi host. The gateway holds the controller's RWS credentials and is trusted by every client, so the attacker can move the robot, load RAPID code and serve false camera frames to all inference clients.
threats.mitigation: Implemented: the gateway runs in a container with only port 8000 exposed by the application. Remaining: run the container as a non-root user (the Dockerfile sets no USER), pin dependency versions, restrict SSH access to the Pi, apply updates, and monitor the host.

threats.title: Unsafe AI command accepted by the gateway
threats.description: An inference client sends a robot job that is syntactically valid but physically unsafe, for example a target that makes the arm or the gripper strike the table, the tray or the other arm, or an excessive speed. If the gateway forwards it unchecked, the robot executes it.
threats.mitigation: Implemented and tested: targets outside the safe-zone box are refused before anything is written to the controller; speed (1..1500 mm/s), acceleration and ramp are range-checked; one job per arm; RAPID checks reachability with CalcJointT. Remaining: only the target flange position is checked, not the path, the gripper tip or the home move; one box is shared by both arms and there is no arm-to-arm collision check; the maximum speed of 1500 mm/s is far above what picking needs.

threats.title: Gateway service failure
threats.description: The gateway process stops because of a software fault, a container crash, resource exhaustion or loss of the Pi. All inference clients lose both the camera and the robot at once, since the gateway is the only path to either.
threats.mitigation: Implemented: the container restarts automatically after a crash or reboot, and /health reports degraded components. Remaining: there is no watchdog on the robot side; a job already written runs to the end and RAPID keeps running. A safe-stop reaction when the gateway disappears is not implemented.

threats.title: Disclosure of robot state and API structure
threats.description: Robot state, security mode, camera status and the full API description are readable without authentication through /health and the FastAPI documentation pages, which helps an attacker plan an attack.
threats.mitigation: Implemented: /health returns no client ids or tokens. Remaining: disable /docs and /openapi.json on the deployed gateway and limit /health to the supervisor's address.

threats.title: Client impersonation with a stolen or shared token
threats.description: Bearer tokens travel in clear text over HTTP, so anyone who can observe lab traffic can copy one and act as that client. The inference script capture_and_detect.py and the real-robot tests use the operator token (priority 100) rather than the autonomy token, so a token copied from an inference device gives full operator control, including pre-empting any other client's lease.
threats.mitigation: Implemented: strict mode stores only SHA-256 hashes, compares them in constant time, and supports one token per client. Remaining: TLS on the gateway, a separate low-priority token for each inference device, and token rotation.

threats.title: No audit trail of robot jobs and program changes
threats.description: The gateway does not log which client sent which robot job, RAPID module upload, start or stop. After an incident it cannot be shown which client, and therefore which inference platform or person, caused a movement.
threats.mitigation: Implemented: calibration uploads record updated_by and updated_at. Remaining: an append-only log of every state-changing request with time, client id, request body and result, kept outside the container.

threats.title: Arbitrary RAPID code loaded through the gateway
threats.description: Any client with robot.control and the lease, which includes the autonomy role used by inference clients, can upload a RAPID module, start and stop the program. Uploaded RAPID code runs on the controller and is not limited by the gateway's safe zone, so a compromised inference client can escalate from sending checked jobs to running unchecked robot code.
threats.mitigation: Implemented: the upload requires robot.control and the lease, and is refused while RAPID runs. Remaining: a separate permission for program changes given only to the operator, an allow-list or hash check of the permitted modules, or disabling the route in production.

threats.title: Legacy command route bypasses gateway validation
threats.description: The deprecated POST /robot/command forwards free-form text to the team's CommServer socket server without applying the gateway's safe zone or speed limits. CommServer's own limits are +/-1000 mm, much wider than the gateway's box.
threats.mitigation: Implemented: the route is marked deprecated and logs a warning. Remaining: remove the route and the CommServer task once no client depends on them, or parse and check the command against the same safe zone.

threats.title: Lapsed control lease leaves the robot moving
threats.description: The lease expires only when it is next read; there is no timer. If the controlling client crashes or loses the network, the job it sent runs to the end, RAPID keeps running and nothing moves the robot to a safe state or tells the next platform to take over.
threats.mitigation: Planned (gateway/TODO.md): a background watchdog that reacts to a lapsed lease, for example by stopping RAPID, homing, or refusing new jobs until control is acquired again. The reaction has not been decided.

threats.title: Development mode enabled on the deployed gateway
threats.description: In development mode the gateway trusts the X-Dev-Client header and checks no token, so any device on the network can act as the operator. The example configuration file sets development mode, and the configuration is built into the image.
threats.mitigation: Implemented: the code default is strict and the deployed Pi gateway uses strict mode. Remaining: refuse to start in development mode when listening on a non-loopback address, and show the mode in the start-up log.

threats.title: Request flooding of the gateway
threats.description: There is no rate limiting. Repeated requests for full-resolution RGB (about 6 MB per frame) and depth frames, or many lease and status requests, load the Pi's CPU and network, which it shares with the secondary inference client.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: per-client rate limits, smaller frames on request, and network rules on the Lynx so that only known clients reach port 8000.

threats.title: Unauthenticated client sends robot jobs
threats.description: A device on the lab network that has no token calls the gateway API to read the camera or move the robot.
threats.mitigation: Implemented and tested (test_auth.py): in strict mode every route except /health requires a valid bearer token, and unknown or missing tokens are rejected before any route runs. A missing or malformed registry stops the gateway from starting.

threats.title: Read-only client performs control actions
threats.description: A client registered for diagnostics only (robot.read, camera.read) tries to move the robot, change RAPID or upload calibration.
threats.mitigation: Implemented and tested: every state-changing route requires robot.control (403 otherwise) and the control lease (409 otherwise).

threats.title: Conflicting jobs from several clients
threats.description: Two inference platforms, or an inference platform and the operator, send jobs to the same arm at the same time, so the robot executes an interleaved and unpredictable sequence.
threats.mitigation: Implemented and tested (test_control.py, test_rws.py): only the holder of the single control lease may send jobs, a strictly higher priority pre-empts, and a busy arm refuses a new job with 409.

data.name:
OAK-D Pro W PoE
camera
data.description: Luxonis OAK-D Pro W PoE RGB-D camera above the workspace, powered over PoE from the Lynx. Accepts one DepthAI connection at a time; the gateway holds it.

threats.title: Compromised camera
threats.description: An attacker gains control of the camera firmware and alters the RGB-D data. Every inference platform reads the same camera through the gateway, so all three can be misled at once and failover gives no protection.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: keep the camera firmware and DepthAI version known and updated, and isolate the camera port on the Lynx. Implemented: the gateway safe zone limits where a misled client can send the robot.

threats.title: False scene presented to the camera
threats.description: Objects, markers or lighting are placed in the scene so that the model detects cups that are not there or misplaces real ones, and the robot is sent to grip at the wrong place.
threats.mitigation: Implemented in capture_and_detect.py: confidence threshold 0.5, a cup is accepted only as a CUP BASE inside a detected CUP, cups outside the reachable area are skipped, and grip heights are fixed. The gateway safe zone bounds the result. Remaining: temporal consistency checks.

threats.title: Camera connection taken by another device
threats.description: The camera accepts only one DepthAI connection. Another device on the network that connects first, or floods the camera, leaves the gateway without images and stops picking.
threats.mitigation: Implemented: the gateway reconnects in the background (5 attempts 5 s apart, then every 60 s) and reports the camera as disconnected on /health. Remaining: restrict which ports may reach the camera on the Lynx.

threats.title: Spoofed camera on the network
threats.description: The gateway connects to the camera by IP address only. A device that takes the camera's link-local address can feed fabricated RGB-D frames to the gateway, and through it to every inference client.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: check the camera's device id (MxId) when connecting, and use port security or static address binding on the Lynx.

data.name:
ABB YuMi IRC5
controller
(RWS, RAPID)
data.description: ABB YuMi IRB 14000 with IRC5 controller, RobotWare 6.16. Robot Web Services 1.0 on port 80 with digest authentication; RAPID tasks T_ROB_L and T_ROB_R run the arm loops; the team's CommServer socket server listens on TCP port 5001 in the communication task.

threats.title: Direct robot commands that bypass the gateway
threats.description: The controller accepts RWS requests with the default account and CommServer commands with no authentication at all. Any device on the robot network can therefore move the robot, load RAPID code or stop the program without going through the gateway and its checks.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: change the default RWS account and password and give the gateway its own user with only the rights it needs, retire CommServer, and isolate the controller's port on the Lynx so that only the gateway host can reach it.

threats.title: Gateway compromise gives robot control
threats.description: Because the gateway is the trusted path to the robot and holds the RWS credentials, an attacker who controls the gateway controls the robot.
threats.mitigation: See threat 19 for hardening the gateway. Remaining on the robot side: SafeMove or equivalent controller-level limits that do not depend on the gateway.

threats.title: Arm tasks do not check the workspace themselves
threats.description: The RAPID arm loops execute any reachable target written to their variables. All workspace checking is in the gateway, so a value written by any other RWS client is executed without a safe-zone check.
threats.mitigation: Implemented: RAPID checks reachability with CalcJointT and reports move_ok. Remaining: a workspace check in the arm modules or in the controller's safety configuration, as defence in depth.

threats.title: Unauthorised device on the robot network
threats.description: A person with physical access connects a device to a free Lynx port or the controller's service port and reaches the robot directly.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: lock unused Lynx ports, keep the cell in a controlled area, and restrict access to the controller's service port.

threats.title: Controller actions cannot be attributed
threats.description: All RWS requests from the gateway, rapidctl.py and RobotStudio use the same default account, so the controller's event log cannot show which program or person loaded code or moved the robot.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: separate RWS users for the gateway and for developers, together with the gateway audit log (threat 53).

threats.title: Program stopped or mastership held by another client
threats.description: Another RWS client, the FlexPendant or RobotStudio stops RAPID or holds mastership. Gateway jobs then fail with 409 or 503 and picking stops.
threats.mitigation: Implemented: the gateway reports the RAPID state on /health and refuses jobs with a clear error. Remaining: restrict RWS access as in threat 11.

data.name:
Pi inference client
(secondary)
data.description: capture_and_detect.py with YOLO11n-seg (best.pt, Ultralytics) on the Raspberry Pi 5. Reads RGB-D frames from the gateway, computes cup positions with a local hand-eye calibration file and sends RWS jobs to the gateway.

threats.title: Compromise of the Pi inference client
threats.description: An attacker gains access to the inference process or the Pi. Because the gateway runs on the same Pi, this also exposes the gateway's configuration and token registry, and the operator token the script uses.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: run the inference client under its own user or container, give it its own low-priority token, and restrict SSH access to the Pi.

threats.title: Generation of unsafe commands
threats.description: Wrong detections, a wrong calibration or a software fault make the client send targets that are reachable but wrong, so the gripper collides with the tray, a cup or the other arm.
threats.mitigation: Implemented: the client skips cups outside its picking area and outside a plausible height, uses fixed grip heights and moves the right arm only after the left has left the picking area; the gateway safe zone bounds every target. Remaining: see threat 20.

threats.title: Tampered model weights or client configuration
threats.description: Someone replaces best.pt, the NCNN files or the constants in the script. A .pt file is a Python pickle, so loading a tampered file can also execute arbitrary code on the Pi.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: record and check a hash of the deployed weight files, keep them read-only, and load weights only from the project repository.

threats.title: Disclosure of stored images and detections
threats.description: The client saves every RGB and depth image, annotated image and detection file to disk. Anyone with access to the Pi can read them. The images show only the cell and the cups.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: limit access to the output folder and delete old captures.

threats.title: Raspberry Pi resource exhaustion and overheating
threats.description: Inference takes about 1 s per frame on the Pi, which reached 86 degC without a fan, and the Pi also runs the gateway. Overload or thermal throttling slows both inference and the gateway.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: add cooling, set CPU and memory limits on the containers, and report the Pi's temperature on /health.

threats.title: Pi inference client unavailable
threats.description: The client stops because of a crash, a power loss or a network fault, and the secondary platform is lost.
threats.mitigation: Planned: a supervisor that watches /health and the clients and hands control to the Lynx client. Automatic failover is not implemented yet; today a person starts the next client.

data.name:
Cloud inference
client (primary)
MacBook stand-in
data.description: Primary inference platform. Intended as a cloud service; in the lab a MacBook Pro (Apple M4) on the lab network stands in for it. Runs the same client as the Pi (PyTorch weights).

threats.title: Compromise of the cloud model environment
threats.description: An attacker gains access to the cloud account, the virtual machine or the stand-in laptop, and can change the model, its outputs, or use its token to control the robot.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: strong authentication on the cloud account, a dedicated token with the autonomy role only, and monitoring. The gateway checks (threat 20) still apply to its jobs.

threats.title: Generation of unsafe commands
threats.description: The cloud model sends targets that are syntactically valid but wrong because of a model error or unexpected input.
threats.mitigation: Implemented: the same client-side filters as on the Pi and the gateway safe zone. Remaining: see threat 20.

threats.title: Camera images stored in the cloud
threats.description: Images and detections sent to or stored in the cloud are exposed if the cloud account is accessed by someone else. The images show the cell, and could show people working in it.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: send only what the model needs, store nothing by default, and restrict access to the cloud storage.

threats.title: Disclosure of robot jobs in cloud logs
threats.description: Generated jobs and debug logs kept in the cloud reveal how the system behaves.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: restrict access to logs and keep them only as long as needed.

threats.title: Cloud model unavailable
threats.description: An internet or cloud-provider outage, or a stopped laptop, removes the primary platform.
threats.mitigation: Planned: the supervisor detects the loss and hands control to the Pi client. Automatic failover is not implemented yet.

threats.title: Excessive resource consumption in the cloud
threats.description: Unexpected load or malicious requests consume the cloud resources and delay inference.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: resource limits and monitoring on the cloud service.

data.name:
Lynx inference
client (tertiary)
data.description: Tertiary platform: the client (NCNN export, 320x320 or 640x640 input) packaged as a .wmopkg container for WeOS Application Hosting on the Lynx switch. capture_and_detect.py selects the NCNN model when PICKER_DEVICE=lynx.

threats.title: Compromise of the Lynx container or switch
threats.description: An attacker gains access to the Lynx container or to the WeOS management interface. Because the Lynx also switches all lab traffic and powers the camera, a compromised switch can mirror or redirect every flow in the diagram and cut the camera's power.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: change default management credentials, disable unused management services, restrict management access to one port, and install only signed .wmopkg packages. The Lynx configuration is not documented in the repository yet.

threats.title: Generation of unsafe commands
threats.description: The Lynx client sends wrong targets because of the lower input resolution, inference errors or faults in the application.
threats.mitigation: Implemented: the gateway safe zone and client-side filters. Remaining: see threat 20.

threats.title: Disclosure of model outputs
threats.description: Detections and logs on the Lynx are exposed through the WeOS management interface or a misconfiguration.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: restrict management access and keep no unnecessary logs.

threats.title: Resource exhaustion on the Lynx
threats.description: Hosted applications share a capped part of the switch's CPU and memory. Inference on a 640x640 input took about 5 s and the application has stopped after several frames in live mode, so the last fallback may not keep up.
threats.mitigation: Implemented: a 320x320 export reduces inference to about 1.2 s. Remaining: find and fix the cause of the stops, and set the hosting resource limit deliberately.

threats.title: Lynx inference client unavailable
threats.description: The Lynx client stops and no inference platform is left.
threats.mitigation: Planned: if no platform is available the system goes to a safe stop. This depends on the supervisor and the lease watchdog (threat 56), which are not implemented.

data.name: Operator
data.description: A person using the gateway's scripts (rws_move.py, basic_client.py, capture_and_detect.py) with the operator token, priority 100.

threats.title: Shared operator identity
threats.description: Several people and scripts use the same operator token, so the gateway cannot tell who sent a command even once logging exists.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: one token per person and per inference device, with the audit log of threat 53.

data.name:
Supervisor /
diagnostics client
data.description: Reads /health to select the inference platform. The supervisory failover function is planned; today /health is read by people and the test harness.

data.name:
Developer
workstation
data.description: Builds the gateway image for linux/arm64 and copies it to the Pi with scp; manages the RAPID program with rapid/rapidctl.py directly over RWS.

data.name:
Client token registry
(auth_clients.json)
data.description: SHA-256 hashes of the client tokens with permissions and priority. Loaded once at start-up. Tracked in git and built into the image.

threats.title: Registry altered to add a client or permissions
threats.description: Someone with write access to the image or the Pi adds a token or gives an existing client the '*' permission, and so gains control of the robot.
threats.mitigation: Implemented: the file is validated at start-up and edits need a restart. Remaining: mount it read-only from the host instead of baking it into the image, and review changes in git.

threats.title: Token hashes exposed
threats.description: The hashes are in git and in every image. Unsalted SHA-256 hashes of guessable tokens could be reversed offline.
threats.mitigation: Implemented: generate_token.py creates 256-bit random tokens, which cannot be found from their hashes in practice.

data.name:
Gateway configuration
(.env)
data.description: GATEWAY_* settings: security mode, device addresses, RWS account, safe zone, speed defaults, lease time. Built into the image (no .dockerignore).

threats.title: Configuration changed to weaken protections
threats.description: A changed .env switches to development mode, widens the safe zone or points the gateway at another controller, without any code change.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: mount the file read-only from the host, log the effective settings at start-up, and refuse values outside fixed limits.

threats.title: Secrets built into the container image
threats.description: The image contains .env with the RWS account and auth_clients.json. Image files are saved on development PCs and copied with scp, so anyone with a copy of the image has the controller credentials.
threats.mitigation: Planned (gateway/TODO.md): mount .env and the registry from the host instead of copying them into the image.

data.name:
Calibration store
(calibration.json)
data.description: Camera-to-robot calibration uploaded through POST /calibration and written atomically to a file in the container. capture_and_detect.py currently uses its own local copy.

threats.title: Tampered hand-eye calibration
threats.description: A changed calibration, in the gateway store or in the client's local file, shifts every computed target. The robot then grips at the wrong place, still inside the safe zone.
threats.mitigation: Implemented: uploads need robot.control and the lease and record updated_by. Remaining: one authoritative calibration with a checksum, and a plausibility check after each update.

threats.title: Corrupt calibration file stops the gateway
threats.description: A corrupt calibration file stops the gateway at start-up.
threats.mitigation: Implemented: writes are atomic, so a crash during a write leaves the old file. Remaining: keep a backup copy and fall back to it.

data.name: RGB-D frames (DepthAI, TCP/IP)
data.description: RGB and aligned 16-bit depth at 4 fps over the lab network through the Lynx.

threats.title: Manipulated RGB-D data in transit
threats.description: An attacker on the network path alters frames between the camera and the gateway, so that every client computes wrong cup positions.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: isolate the camera on its own port or VLAN on the Lynx. DepthAI offers no integrity protection. Implemented: the gateway safe zone bounds the consequences.

threats.title: Camera feed interception
threats.description: The unencrypted stream reveals the cell and anything in view.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: network isolation as for threat 6.

threats.title: Acting on a stale or missing camera image
threats.description: The stream stops because of a network fault, PoE loss or interference, and clients compute jobs from an image that no longer matches the scene.
threats.mitigation: Implemented and tested: the gateway answers 503 instead of serving a frame older than 5 s, reconnects to the camera in the background and reports it on /health. The loss of the stream itself still stops picking.

data.name: RWS jobs, RAPID control (HTTP :80)
data.description: Writes per-arm PERS variables and starts or stops RAPID through Robot Web Services, polling for completion every 50 ms. Digest authentication.

threats.title: Robot jobs modified in transit
threats.description: RWS runs over plain HTTP. Digest authentication protects the password but not the content, so a device on the path can change a target after the gateway has checked it.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: isolate the gateway-to-controller link on the Lynx (own VLAN or a direct cable). RobotWare 6 RWS has no TLS on the service port.

threats.title: Replay of captured RWS requests
threats.description: Captured RWS requests are sent again to repeat a movement out of context.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: network isolation as for threat 12; restrict the RWS account.

threats.title: Loss of communication with the controller
threats.description: A cable, network or controller fault cuts the link. The gateway cannot send jobs or learn their outcome.
threats.mitigation: Implemented: 503 when unreachable, 504 after 60 s, reachability on /health. Remaining: the arm finishes its current job with no heartbeat from the gateway; a RAPID-side timeout would stop it.

threats.title: Eavesdropping on robot traffic
threats.description: Plain HTTP reveals jobs, robot state and the RWS user name.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: network isolation as for threat 12.

data.name: Legacy socket commands (TCP :5001, deprecated)
data.description: POST /robot/command forwards the raw command text to the team's CommServer.

threats.title: Unauthenticated legacy socket interface
threats.description: CommServer accepts plain-text commands from anyone who can connect to port 5001 and replies without authentication or integrity protection.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: stop the CommServer task once the RWS route has replaced it (see threats 11 and 55).

data.name: Camera frames (HTTP)
data.description: GET /camera/rgb, /camera/depth, /camera/intrinsics with a bearer token.

data.name: Robot jobs, lease (HTTP)
data.description: Control lease, POST /robot/rws/move|home|gripper and status polling. Uses the Pi's network address, so traffic stays on the host.

threats.title: Modified Pi client jobs
threats.description: Jobs between the Pi client and the gateway are altered. Both run on the same Pi, so this needs access to the host (see threat 40).
threats.mitigation: Implemented: the gateway validates every job regardless of its source.

data.name: Camera frames (HTTP)
data.description: Frames from the gateway to the Lynx client through the switch.

threats.title: Frames to the Lynx client modified or read
threats.description: Frames sent over plain HTTP are read or altered by a device on the path.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: TLS on the gateway (threat 52).

data.name: Robot jobs, lease (HTTP)
data.description: Control lease and RWS jobs from the Lynx client.

threats.title: Modified Lynx client jobs in transit
threats.description: Jobs from the Lynx client are altered on the way to the gateway.
threats.mitigation: Implemented: the gateway validates every job. Remaining: TLS.

threats.title: Token and jobs readable on the network
threats.description: The bearer token and jobs travel in clear text and can be copied.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: TLS and a dedicated low-priority token (threat 52).

threats.title: Lynx client cut off from the gateway
threats.description: The link between the Lynx client and the gateway is interrupted.
threats.mitigation: Planned: a safe stop when no platform holds the lease (threat 56).

data.name: Camera frames (HTTP)
data.description: Frames from the gateway to the primary platform. Crosses the internet boundary in the intended deployment.

threats.title: Camera images exposed over the internet
threats.description: In the intended deployment images cross the internet. Without TLS anyone on the path can read them.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: TLS, or a VPN between the lab and the cloud; send only the image size the model needs.

threats.title: Frames modified on the way to the cloud
threats.description: Frames altered on the internet path make the primary model compute wrong targets.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: TLS with certificate validation. Implemented: gateway safe zone.

data.name: Robot jobs, lease (HTTP)
data.description: Control lease and RWS jobs from the primary platform. Plain HTTP in the lab.

threats.title: Cloud jobs modified in transit
threats.description: Jobs from the cloud model are changed on the internet path before the gateway receives them.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: TLS with certificate validation. Implemented: the gateway validates every job.

threats.title: Token exposed on the internet path
threats.description: The bearer token travels with every request. Exposed on the internet, it lets anyone act as the cloud client.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: TLS, and a token with the lowest priority that can still control the robot.

threats.title: Cloud link unavailable
threats.description: An internet outage cuts the primary platform off from the gateway.
threats.mitigation: Planned: failover to the Pi client. Not implemented yet.

data.name: Operator requests (HTTP, token)
data.description: Moves, RAPID program control and calibration uploads from the operator's scripts.

threats.title: Operator token readable on the network
threats.description: The operator token has the highest priority and travels in clear text.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: TLS on the gateway (threat 52).

data.name: Health status (GET /health, no auth)
data.description: Gateway, camera and controller state.

threats.title: Spoofed health status misleads failover
threats.description: The planned supervisor will choose the platform from /health, which is unauthenticated plain HTTP. A forged answer could trigger or block a failover.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: authenticate the supervisor's health requests or serve them over TLS before failover depends on them.

data.name: Image and configuration (scp, docker load)
data.description: The image is built on a PC for linux/arm64, saved to a file, copied to the Pi and loaded.

threats.title: Tampered gateway image or dependencies
threats.description: Dependencies are not pinned and the image file is not signed or checked on the Pi, so a changed package or a swapped file ends up running as the gateway.
threats.mitigation: Remaining: pin versions in requirements.txt (planned), record the image digest and check it before loading; generate-container.py can sign the .wmopkg for the Lynx.

data.name: RAPID upload (rapidctl.py, RWS)
data.description: rapidctl.py backs up, loads and starts the RAPID program directly over RWS, without the gateway.

threats.title: RAPID program changed outside the gateway
threats.description: RAPID modules can be loaded with the default RWS account from any PC, so the program the gateway relies on can change without the gateway or its users knowing.
threats.mitigation: Implemented: rapidctl.py backs up the replaced modules and asks before changing a real controller. Remaining: a dedicated developer account and a check of the loaded modules' hashes by the gateway at start-up.

data.description: Read once at start-up.

data.description: Read once at start-up.

data.description: Atomic write on upload, read at start-up.
